label: gate1_r3
inputs_read: title: 利率没动，只改了一句话
why: Line #1 (听说下周涨价，你今天就买了) is about me. I do this with 618 and Double 11 presales, so I stop to see where it goes. It does read a bit like an ad opener, though. If the frame looks like a shopping ad, half my friends would swipe before 3s.
why_8s: #2 matches the title, and #3 adds a weird detail: the Fed just said 'at least until mid-2013' and that alone was news. I want to know how one sentence changes anything. The title's question is still open at 8s, so I stay.
first_moment_I_got_curious: #2 (2.9s) 利率没动，只改了一句话. It's the title come true and I want the trick. Second spike at #20 (75.7s) 计划一次都没用过. That one actually got me.
where_I_would_swipe_away: 12.4-16.0s: no subtitle for 3.6s right after #4. If the screen shows nothing new, this is the most likely place I leave. I just got a cliffhanger (forecasters believed it) and then dead air.

16.0s #5 (2026诺奖：霍尔、伍德福德): a hard turn from the Fed story to a Nobel announcement. People who stayed for the money hook may decide it's a lecture now. I'd stay because the Nobel is hot this week, but it's a coin flip.
31.8s #9 (1970年代…越刺激物价越涨): third time jump in 30s (2011 -> 2026 -> 1982 -> 1970s). I start to lose track of the story.
48.1s #13 (利率降到0，没法再降了): no year, no country. Whose rate? When? It feels like a topic jump. Weak point #2.
84.3s #22 (反过来也一样): the payoff already landed at #20-21 and this feels like a second video starting. With 24s left at 1:24, a lot of people leave here. The 2013 bond part is the most skippable.
lines_I_did_not_understand: #4 加息推到[21个月]以上: 21 months from when? From the announcement? Pushed back from what? I get the gist (they believed rates stay low longer) but not the number.
#9 越刺激物价越涨: who is doing the 刺激? The government? The central bank? And why does it link to Hall's spending idea right before it? There's no bridge.
#13 利率降到0: which country, what year? I assume the US after 2008, but I'm guessing.

#14 伍德福德等人提议：提前说出打算: I only realized later this is the same trick as #2-3 in 2011. The video never says 'this is what the Fed did in 2011', so the callback is missed. If it said that, I'd get an 'oh!' moment.
#19 让西班牙年息少了约[1块]: from 7 to 6? Over how long? It sounds small after 'whatever it takes'. Is 1块 a lot? Tell me it's a lot.
#23 美联储暗示：一直在买的债要少买: why was the Fed buying bonds at all? This is the one line I'd have to rewatch, and I still wouldn't get it.
#24 1.76%涨到2.81%: everything before this was in 块 per 100块 and now it's percentages. Also, is +1 point huge? No feeling for it. '100块年息从1.76块变2.81块' would land better.
#16-17 欧洲央行时任行长: no name. Fine for me, but if he's famous (Draghi?) a name plus a face would make the quote hit harder.
takeaway_in_my_words: Central banks can move money without moving rates. They just say what they plan to do later, and everyone (shoppers, companies, investors) acts on it today. That's why this year's Nobel went to the guys who explained it. It works both ways: one wrong hint can push rates up too.
surprise_that_stuck: #20: the ECB promised to buy Spanish bonds 'if needed', Spain's borrowing cost dropped, and by 2015 they had never used the plan once. Talk alone did the work. This is the line I'd repeat to people. #8 (剩下的多是月光族) also made me laugh. It's me.
title_I_would_click: 利率没动，只改了一句话: yes, I'd click. It's a small mystery (how does one sentence matter?) with no jargon. Only one title was given.
title_that_misleads: Slightly. The title sets up a 2011 Fed story, but that story drops at 12.4s and never gets an explicit ending. Most of the video is Nobel plus the ECB in Spain. It's not clickbait, because the whole video is about 'words move money', but I expected the 2011 case to be the spine and it isn't. Saying at #14 that this is what happened in 2011 would fix it.
what_I_would_comment: 所以“不惜一切代价”这句话值多少钱？西班牙一年省的利息够我月光多少辈子 / 原来我被预售割韭菜也算宏观经济学
tell_a_friend: This year's economics Nobel is basically about how central banks control money with what they say. The ECB said 'we'll do whatever it takes', never actually spent a cent, and Spain's borrowing cost still fell.
score_reason: Strong open (#1-3) and a real payoff (#16-21). I lose points for the 3.6s gap at 12.4s, four time jumps in the first 36s, the unlinked zero-rate line, and a taper section at the end (#22-25) that feels like a second video. 1:48 is long for my feed. I'd likely finish if I'm already curious about the Nobel, and leave around 1:24 if not.

for_frames_only.what_this_says_in_5s: No frames were in my task. I judged only from the subtitles and the title.
